question:
I have image inputs nested inside a richer object, and I want to make sure a custom adapter does not serialize them into marker text before the model sees them. I need to inspect the actual message content blocks, not a stringified approximation.

What matters is both the few-shot example and the live query, because I have seen systems preserve one and flatten the other. I want a tiny offline harness that makes the split explicit.

Give me a complete, runnable Python program that formats one demo plus one live request through an XML-style adapter, prints both user-message contents, and asserts that the demo keeps three structured image blocks, the live request keeps one, and no custom-type sentinel text leaks through.
gold_answer:
```python
import pydantic

import dspy


class ImageWrapper(pydantic.BaseModel):
    images: list[dspy.Image]
    tag: list[str]


class MySig(dspy.Signature):
    image: ImageWrapper = dspy.InputField()
    text: str = dspy.OutputField()


def count_image_blocks(content):
    if not isinstance(content, list):
        return 0
    return sum(1 for item in content if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') == 'image_url')


demo_wrapper = ImageWrapper(
    images=[
        dspy.Image('https://example.com/1.jpg'),
        dspy.Image('https://example.com/2.jpg'),
        dspy.Image('https://example.com/3.jpg'),
    ],
    tag=['demo'],
)
query_wrapper = ImageWrapper(images=[dspy.Image('https://example.com/4.jpg')], tag=['query'])

demos = [dspy.Example(image=demo_wrapper, text='demo text')]
messages = dspy.XMLAdapter().format(MySig, demos, {'image': query_wrapper})

print(messages[1]['content'])
print(messages[-1]['content'])

assert count_image_blocks(messages[1]['content']) == 3
assert count_image_blocks(messages[-1]['content']) == 1
assert 'CUSTOM-TYPE-START-IDENTIFIER' not in str(messages)
```

rubric.statement: The program defines a nested wrapper model whose `images` field is `list[dspy.Image]`, and uses that wrapper as the `image` input field of a DSPy signature.

The harness constructs one few-shot demo wrapper holding three images and one live-query wrapper holding one image, wraps the demo with `dspy.Example`, and formats them with `dspy.XMLAdapter().format(...)`.

It directly inspects the user-message `content` entries at `messages[1]` and `messages[-1]`, using the structured content-block lists returned after custom-type splitting rather than a single flattened prompt string.
The demo-side check distinguishes three preserved structured `image_url` blocks for the three example images in the few-shot user message.
The live-query check distinguishes a single preserved structured `image_url` block for the query image in the final user message.

The program asserts that no `CUSTOM-TYPE-START-IDENTIFIER` marker text remains in the formatted messages, reflecting that custom-type sentinel serialization is converted back into content blocks before the final user messages are returned.
